heading: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - WAITING AREA - MORNING

units.text: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - WAITING AREA - MORNING
Fluorescent lights.
A row of molded chairs.
A ficus that died years ago and has not been told.
Deb, 60s, reception, bifocals, a mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST GRANDMA, taps at a keyboard behind scratched plexiglass.
She doesn't look up when the door opens.
A man comes in.
He is tall, late forties, a gray work jacket zipped to the throat, a folder pressed to his ribs like a shield.
He stands very still just inside the door, as if the room might reject him.
THE MAN waits.
Name?
units.name: DEB

units.text: I have a nine o'clock.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Name.
units.name: DEB

units.text: He says nothing for a second.
She finally looks at him.
Is Officer Okafor in?
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Honey, everybody's in. It's nine in the morning. Sit.
units.name: DEB

units.text: He sits.
He keeps the folder on his knees.
Across the room, a clock ticks, slower than a clock should.
